Subject: Quick Qs on where EU customer data is processed

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams asked for a short Q&A so we can finish our inbound vendor risk review. Can you confirm the following for EU customers (specifically for patients' PHI-derived prompts and generated outputs):

- Where requests are executed (region names / cloud zones) and whether any request/response data leaves the EU for processing.
- A current list of subprocessors that might see or touch request payloads (including logging/telemetry vendors).
- What contractual transfer mechanism you rely on (SCCs, adequacy, etc.) and whether you have an EU data processing Addendum we can sign.
- Retention and deletion timelines: how quickly can we purge prompt/context and derived embeddings, and what about logs/backups?
- Any controls around Redwood staff access to content and whether model weights or third-party models are hosted outside the EU.

Appreciate a concise answer we can share with our security folks. If you have an evidence pack or diagram, that would help.

Oliver

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where EU customer data is processed

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Below is an operational summary and a few links to artifacts; happy to hop on a quick call if needed. I copied our security lead, Rishi, and Marissa from our account team.

High-level summary (for EU customers):
- Execution locations: Hosted Redwood API customers in the EU are processed in our eu-central-1 region (Frankfurt) by default. We also offer eu-west-1 (Ireland) on request; both are isolated within AWS EU zones.
- Cross-border transfers: Routine inference for EU-region tenants stays within EU compute (no outbound processing to the US). Non-production telemetry, analytics, and some CI/CD tooling operate from our US infrastructure but are pseudonymized/aggregated and do not contain patient PHI. For customers who require zero-export guarantees we offer Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Subprocessors (short list): AWS (EU regions for compute; us-east-1 for some control-plane ops), Cloudflare (edge routing; EU POPs used where available), Datadog (telemetry; telemetry sampled/PII redacted), Sentry (exceptions), Google Workspace (docs), and Fastly for CDN in some edge configurations. Full inventory attached.
- Transfer mechanism: We operate under a standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) which includes EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and the UK Addendum where applicable. We can provide a countersigned DPA; there is also an existing Data Processing Impact Assessment (DPIA) overview for healthcare customers.
- Retention & deletion (standard hosted):
  - Inference cache / KV: ephemeral; per-session data is evicted immediately after session termination (typically within seconds to minutes).
  - Customer data retention window (log/trace): operational traces and request logs are retained for 90 days for security and billing purposes, then purged.
  - Backups & snapshots: encrypted backups are rotated and retained up to 30 days; longer retention policies are by contract for Dedicated/Private.
  - Deletion process: we expose an API for account-level purge requests; upon receipt we schedule immediate removal from active stores and a deletion sweep that completes within 72 hours for primary stores and 30 days for backups/snapshots. We can accelerate this to contractually bound SLAs for enterprise agreements.
- Staff access & models: Redwood staff access to raw request payloads is limited to a small ops/security team under strict RBAC and just-in-time access with audit logging. Model weights for open-source models are stored in the same region as execution when running under EU tenants. For hosted customers, we may serve open-source models that we host; if a customer requires certified on-prem or EU-only model hosting, we support that in Private/Dedicated.

Evidence & links: attached is a curated subprocessor inventory and a topology diagram showing execution paths. Additional artifacts: DPA + SCC template, DPIA summary. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/crestwave-evidence/DP-map

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-inventory-202703.pdf; data-processing-map-crestwave.png

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Processing & transfer details for EU customer — Crestwave follow-up

Kim / Marissa — looping in quick notes and proposed collateral for Oliver / Crestwave Legal: 

- Confirmations for Oliver's questions:
  * Control-plane: control-plane telemetry (billing signals, deployment metadata) originate from our US control plane but do NOT include plaintext prompt/response bodies for EU tenants. Any telemetry containing sensitive tokens is redacted at ingestion; we use deterministic hashing for identifiers.
  * Telemetry vendors: Datadog and Sentry only receive truncated/obfuscated traces. We have pipeline rules (ingest filters) stripping fields labeled as PII/PHI; samples are reviewed under strict access controls. Documentation is in the attached inventory.
  * Backups SLA: we can meet a 7-day maximum for backup retention in a tailored enterprise DPA for Crestwave (requires contract amendment).
  * Staff access: JIT access with ticketed approvals and immutable audit logs. We can provide a redacted access log sample for due diligence.

- Action items:
  1) Marissa, please prepare a 1-page evidence pack (DPA + SCC extract, DPIA summary, redacted access log sample) and the topology PNG for the legal team. Attach the DPA and a countersign option in HubSpot (deal CRW-4721).
  2) Kim, propose a 30-minute technical call with Oliver and their privacy lead. Rishi can join to answer telemetry/ingress questions.

Thanks — I'll draft the short bullets into a slide we can share.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Product Manager
Redwood Inference
